plan: This auction mechanism functions as a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of the ascending clock mechanics. In such formats, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding above value risks losing money if you win at a price above your value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $36.

This auction mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my own bid only determines when I exit, not what I pay (if I win). In second-price auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I never overpay since I pay based on others' bids, not mine. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $33.

Since the payment rule is equivalent to a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), bidding my true value is a dominant strategy. There's no benefit to shading up or down: bidding above value risks paying more than the prize is worth, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
